newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: ZCCM indemnified from environmental abuse.
newsitem.headline: ZCCM indemnified from environmental abuse.

text.p: Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) has been indemnified from environmental offences to help with the privatisation of the company, environment minister William Harrington said on Thursday.

Harrington told Reuters the Zambian government had waived legal clauses that made the mining conglomerate, which earns about 90 percent of Zambia's foreign receipts, liable under Zambian environmental laws.
"The clauses were waived to facilitate the privatisation of the mines. Investors do not want to be held liable for practices introduced by ZCCM in the past," Harrington said.
He was responding to calls by a parliamentary environmental workshop this week which urged tougher government action against ZCCM to force it to adopt better waste disposal methods.
The workshop heard of complaints by residents in the northern Copperbelt province of pollution from ZCCM mines.
Residents were particularly concerned with sulphur dioxide emissions which they said destroyed vegetation and damaged buildings in mining townships.
The emissions were also blamed for an increase in skin and respiratory diseases in nearby mining towns.
The Environmental Council of Zambia has estimated that 200,000 tonnes of sulphur dioxide are discharged by ZCCM per year.

Colonial laws indemnified mining companies from prosecution under environmental laws, but last year the government amended the law to make ZCCM liable for environmental pollution. It later waived the amended law at the prodding of prospective investors.
The company is for sale under an ambitious government privatisation programme. Detailed bids for ZCCM assets, which will be sold in nine packages, will be made next month.
